identity.title: Optical tomography of the born-again ejecta of A 58

paper_type_evidence.quote: In order to peer into the morpho-kinematics of the H-deficient ejecta in the born-again PN A 58, we present the first integral field spectroscopic observations of a born-again PN as obtained with GTC MEGARA.
In combination with ALMA and Hubble Space Telescope data we are able to produce a complete view of the H-deficient ionized and molecular ejecta in A 58.
These observations correspond to project 2019.1.01408.S (PI: D. Tafoya) and their details can be found in Tafoya et al. (2022).

claims.hypothesis: The optical emission of the born-again ejecta in A 58 shares the same disk-plus-jet physical structure and kinematics as the ALMA CO molecular emission or a simple expanding sphere.
claims.experiment: Compare sub-resolution 2D Gaussian channel centroids of GTC MEGARA [O III] and [N II] emission lines with HST imaging and ALMA CO (J=3->2) moment maps, and model the 3D geometry using SHAPE.
claims.result: Optical emission centroids in the disk velocity range have the opposite spatial velocity orientation to the CO disk, extend to higher velocities (-300 to +200 km s^-1) than CO HVCs (-140 to +140 km s^-1), and trace a loop at high blueshifted velocities.
claims.finding: The molecular disk does not emit optically but obscures the rear optical lobe; the ionized gas instead forms a thick hourglass bipolar outflow that embraces the molecular high-velocity components.

claims.hypothesis: H-alpha emission is present in the H-deficient born-again ejecta of A 58 rather than being He II 6560 contamination.
claims.experiment: Extract high-dispersion GTC MEGARA spectra of the central ejecta in H-alpha and He II 4686, subtracting surrounding nebular emission.
claims.result: Blueshifted emission is detected in H-alpha while He II 4686 is not detected, ruling out He II 6560 contamination.
claims.finding: H-alpha emission from the born-again ejecta is unambiguously detected for the first time, with only the blue component visible due to dust extinction of the red component by the disk.

evidence.quote: We emphasize that the non-detection of the He ii λ4686 emission line discards the possible contribution of He ii λ6560 to the emission bluewards of Hα, which is thus confidently attributed to the ejecta.

evidence.quote: Instead an arbitrary emission law has been included in the model to simulate both the effects of extinction (emission decreasing with the optical depth along the line of sight and very particularly behind the molecular disk) and distance to the CSPN (emission decreasing with radial distance to the CSPN).

referee_caveats_inferred: 2D Gaussian centroiding per velocity channel assumes a single dominant emission peak per channel; if both lobes of the hourglass or clumpy structures contribute simultaneously at a given velocity, the single-Gaussian centroid will reflect a flux-weighted blend rather than a physical structure's location.

The alignment between ALMA, HST, and MEGARA relies on matching the optical continuum centroid, the HST F547M peak, and the ALMA center, which may be affected by severe, wavelength-dependent dust scattering and extinction near V605 Aql.
The SHAPE model is qualitative and relies on an unparameterized ad hoc extinction/emission law rather than radiative transfer.
